segments.text:
I Suppoſe that the afflicciōs of this life, are not worthye of the glory which ſhalbe ſhewed vpon vs. For the feruent deſyre of the creature abideth, loking when the ſonnes of god ſhal appeare, becauſe the creature is ſubdued to vanitie againſt the will therof, but for his will which hath ſubdued the ſame in hope. For the ſame creature ſhalbe deliuered from the bōdage of corrupcion, into the glorious libertie of the ſonnes of GOD. For we knowe that euery creature groneth with vs alſo, and trauayleth in payne, euen vnto thys tyme: not onely it, but we alſo whiche haue the
firſt fruites of the ſpirite, mourne in our ſelues alſo, & waite for the adopcion (of the children of GOD) euen the deliueraunce of our bodies.
